title: The De Rham Complex Homotopy and Mayer Vietoris

items.title: De rham cochain complex
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold M, define the real cochain complex Ω•(M), with d of degree +1 and zero terms for k<0 or k>dim M. Boundaryless unless explicitly stated; the interval calculation uses smooth forms up to its endpoints.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Closed and exact differential forms
items.statement: Z^k=ker(d:Ω^k→Ω^{k+1}), B^k=im(d:Ω^{k-1}→Ω^k); exact means in B, closed means in Z. Since d²=0, B⊂Z, including B^0=0.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (2014)

items.title: De rham cohomology
items.statement: H^k_dR(M)=Z^k/B^k, a real vector space; only closed forms have classes.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (2014)

items.title: Zero and out of range de rham cohomology
items.statement: H^k_dR(M)=0 for k<0 or k>dim M; the empty manifold has zero cohomology in every degree.
items.strategy: The cochain terms vanish, hence so do their cycle quotients; on the empty set every form space is the zero vector space.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Zero th de rham cohomology is locally constant functions
items.statement: H^0_dR(M) is the algebra of locally constant real functions; it is R for nonempty connected M.
items.strategy: In a coordinate ball integrate df along a segment using FTC: df=0 implies constancy. Constancy is local and a nonempty level set of a locally constant function is both open and closed on a connected component. B^0=0.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Pullback is a morphism of de rham complexes
items.statement: A smooth F:M→N induces a degree-zero cochain map F*:Ω•(N)→Ω•(M).
items.strategy: Naturality dF*=F*d gives the cochain-map equation, with real linearity inherited from pullback.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Pullback induces a well defined map on de rham cohomology
items.statement: F*[ω]=[F*ω] defines a linear map H^k(N)→H^k(M).
items.strategy: Reindex a cochain complex by C_n=C^{-n} and apply the earlier induced-homology theorem. Closedness and exact changes are preserved because dF*=F*d.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham cohomology is a contravariant functor
items.statement: The de Rham groups define a contravariant functor on smooth manifolds: (G∘F)*=F*∘G* and id*=id.
items.strategy: Apply the earlier homology functor to pullback identities, using the same degree reindexing as the preceding item.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Wedge with a closed form preserves exactness classes
items.statement: For closed α of degree p and β of degree q, dη∧β=d(η∧β) and α∧dθ=(-1)^p d(α∧θ).
items.strategy: Expand the graded Leibniz formula and set dα=dβ=0. Change the two representatives successively, retaining closedness after each change.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Wedge product descends to de rham cohomology
items.statement: [α][β]=[α∧β] is a well-defined bilinear graded-commutative associative product on de Rham cohomology.
items.strategy: The graded Leibniz rule gives closedness and the preceding lemma gives independence of both representatives. Associativity and the sign (-1)^{pq} descend from forms; [1] is the unit.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (2014)

items.title: De rham cohomology ring
items.statement: H•_dR(M), with wedge-induced multiplication and unit [1], is the de Rham cohomology ring, a unital graded-commutative real algebra. The zero ring on the empty manifold is allowed.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Pullback is a homomorphism of de rham cohomology algebras
items.statement: Smooth pullback induces a unital graded algebra homomorphism H•(N)→H•(M).
items.strategy: Apply pullback to wedge products and the constant function 1; then pass to classes.

references.title: Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (2014)
John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Integration along the unit interval for a differential form
items.statement: For smooth ω on M×[0,1], uniquely write ω=α_t+dt∧β_t with tangential forms; define Kω=∫_0^1 β_t dt, degree -1, and K=0 on degree zero. Coefficients are smooth up to endpoints and locally extend across them; integration is in the fixed finite-dimensional fibre.

references.title: Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (2014)
John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The interval homotopy operator is coordinate independent
items.statement: K is coordinate independent and maps smooth forms to smooth forms.
items.strategy: β_t=i_t*(ι_{∂t}ω) is intrinsic. Under changes of M-coordinates the fibre transition matrix is independent of t, hence commutes with integration. On a relatively compact coordinate rectangle iterate the compact-parameter differentiation theorem for every derivative; local smooth extensions handle endpoints.

references.title: Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (2014)
John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham homotopy formula on a product
items.statement: i_1*−i_0*=dK+Kd on all smooth forms on M×[0,1].
items.strategy: Compute dω=d_Mα_t+dt∧(∂_tα_t−d_Mβ_t). Integrating the dt coefficient gives Kdω=α_1−α_0−d_MKω by FTC and parameter differentiation. This also proves the degree-zero and top-degree cases.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham homotopy formula for a smooth homotopy
items.statement: For smooth F:M×[0,1]→N, F_1*−F_0*=d(KF*)+(KF*)d.
items.strategy: Apply the product formula to F*ω and move d through F* by naturality.

references.title: Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (2014)
John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Smoothly homotopic maps induce the same de rham map
items.statement: Smoothly homotopic smooth maps have equal induced de Rham maps in every degree.
items.strategy: Use C_n=C^{-n}; K becomes degree +1 and the product identity is exactly the earlier chain-homotopy equation. Apply its induced-homology theorem.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham cohomology is smooth homotopy invariant
items.statement: A smooth homotopy equivalence induces an isomorphism of de Rham graded algebras.
items.strategy: Apply homotopy invariance to both composites with a specified smooth homotopy inverse and functoriality to obtain both inverse identities.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham cohomology is continuous homotopy invariant on smooth manifolds
items.statement: Under countable choice, continuously homotopic smooth maps induce equal de Rham maps. Continuous homotopy equivalences between smooth manifolds induce inverse de Rham algebra maps via smooth representatives.
items.strategy: Under countable choice, first establish the following local smoothing construction on the boundaryless manifolds of this page. Given continuous F:P→N smooth on an open V containing closed A, use the repaired finite-dimensional embedding theorem under the same countable-choice hypothesis to embed N properly by j=(G,rho) into R^k. No dimension-optimal weak Whitney or generic-projection theorem is used. Construct the Euclidean tube locally as follows; no smooth radius minorant or global tubular-existence theorem is used. For S=j(N), let E(p,v)=p+v on its orthogonal normal bundle. The normal-addition local-diffeomorphism lemma gives a diffeomorphism near each (p,0). The bundle topology is the subspace topology in S×R^k, so some V_a(p)={(q,v):|q-p|<a, |v|<a} lies in such a neighborhood. Define h(p)=sup{a:0<a≤1 and E restricted to V_a(p) is a diffeomorphism onto its image}. This set is nonempty and bounded before the supremum is taken. Eligibility is downward closed; for every a<h(p), a larger eligible radius exists. Hence E is injective and locally invertible throughout V_h(p)(p): each point, or pair of points for injectivity, lies in one smaller eligible V_a(p). If 0<a<h(p)-|p-q| then V_a(q)⊂V_h(p)(p), so a is eligible and h(q)≥a. Supremum and symmetry give |h(p)-h(q)|≤|p-q|, including the case of nonpositive right-hand lower bound. Thus h is positive continuous. On Ω={(p,v):|v|<h(p)/2}, E is a local diffeomorphism. If E(p,v)=E(q,w), order h(q)≤h(p); then |p-q|≤|v|+|w|<(h(p)+h(q))/2≤h(p), and both pairs lie in V_h(p)(p), proving equality. Ω is open; an injective local diffeomorphism is open, and its local smooth inverses agree. Therefore E:Ω→U is a diffeomorphism onto an open neighborhood of S. Set r=π∘E^{-1}; the smooth normal-bundle projection gives a smooth retraction. Countable choice already assumed covers the declared normal-bundle manifold interface; the radius function uses suprema, not simultaneous choices of neighborhoods. Set e(p)=min(1,dist(jF(p),U^c)/2) if U^c is nonempty, and e=1 otherwise. Distance to a nonempty closed set is finite and 1-Lipschitz by the triangle inequality; openness gives positive distance at each jF(p). Hence e is positive continuous and B_e(jF(p)) lies in U. Absolute Euclidean Whitney gives smooth Q with |Q-jF|<e. Construct the cutoff from a subordinate refinement-indexed smooth partition (φ_i) for {V,P\A}, not an assumed two-function output. Assign each support to V if possible, and to P\A otherwise; this is a prescribed two-case rule. Let χ be the sum of the V-assigned functions. Both grouped sums are locally finite smooth sums. Each grouped union of closed supports is closed: near any point only finitely many supports occur, so its complement is locally the complement of a finite closed union. Consequently suppχ is contained in V, while the other grouped support union is closed and disjoint from A. On its open complement χ=1, giving the required neighbourhood of A. Put R=χjF+(1-χ)Q. This is smooth on V and equals Q on a neighbourhood of each point outside suppχ, so is globally smooth. It equals jF near A and |R-jF|=(1-χ)|Q-jF|<e. Therefore G=j^{-1}rR is smooth, agrees with F near A, and j^{-1}r((1-s)jF+sR) is a continuous homotopy F~G rel A, since the entire segment stays in the e-ball. For a continuous homotopy H between smooth f0,f1 set P=M×R, λ(t)=σ(3t-1) using the standard step, F(x,t)=H(x,λ(t)), V=M×((−∞,1/3)∪(2/3,∞)), and A=M×((−∞,1/4]∪[3/4,∞)). F is smooth on V. The construction gives a smooth map on M×R with the exact endpoint collars; restriction to[0,1] and smooth homotopy invariance give equal de Rham maps. Taking A empty and χ=0 also gives a smooth representative of every continuous map, with the explicit straight-line retraction homotopy. For continuous inverse homotopy equivalences f,g, smooth them to f',g'; composition and concatenation give g'f'~id and f'g'~id, and the endpoint construction smooths these homotopies. Thus pullbacks are inverse algebra maps; two smooth representatives of one continuous class likewise induce the same map. Empty sources are immediate, and a map to an empty target forces an empty source. Countable choice covers countable coordinate/partition/approximation/tubular selections; no relative Whitney theorem, continuous-map smoothing corollary or fine-tubular-radius lemma is used. For the countable-choice implementation of the partition suppliers, use the set of all admissible coordinate-ball tuples instead of choosing one tuple for every point. Second countability and countable choice give the needed countable subcover and tuple representatives. In the shrinking proof take each exhaustion index to be the least suitable integer; on each compact annulus take all admissible nested pairs, and use countable choice on the countable family of nonempty sets of finite subcovers, then on the countable family of bump choices. Flatten the supplied finite lists and normalize the locally finite bump sum as in the published partition construction. Thus no uncountable pointwise choice or dependent recursive selection is hidden.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Radial contraction of a star shaped domain
items.statement: For an open U⊂R^n star-shaped about a specified c∈U, F(x,t)=c+t(x−c) is its radial smooth contraction from c to id.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Poincare lemma for differential forms on star shaped domains
items.statement: For k≥1 a closed smooth k-form on a star-shaped open domain is exact. For centre 0 the primitive is (K F*ω)_x(v_1,…,v_{k−1})=∫_0^1 t^{k−1}ω_{tx}(x,v_1,…,v_{k−1})dt.
items.strategy: F_0*ω=0 in positive degree since its differential is zero. The homotopy formula gives ω=dKF*ω. The factor t^{k−1} follows from one parameter vector x and k−1 vectors tv_i; the integrand extends smoothly at t=0, so no division by t or singular endpoint is used.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (2014)

items.title: Closed differential forms are locally exact
items.statement: Every closed smooth form of POSITIVE degree is locally exact.
items.strategy: Choose a coordinate ball, apply the star-shaped result and pull its primitive back. Degree zero is excluded: the nonzero constant function is closed and not exact.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham cohomology of a contractible smooth manifold
items.statement: Under countable choice, a nonempty contractible smooth manifold has H^0=R and H^k=0 for k>0.
items.strategy: The identity is continuously homotopic to a constant smooth map. Their pullbacks agree on cohomology; the constant map has zero pullback in positive degree. Contractibility makes the manifold connected; apply the H^0 computation.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Two open set de rham mayer vietoris cochain maps
items.statement: For M=U∪V with U,V open, rω=(ω|U,ω|V) and s(α,β)=β|U∩V−α|U∩V are cochain maps. This difference sign is fixed throughout.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The de rham mayer vietoris sequence is exact at the first two terms
items.statement: 0→Ω^k(M)→Ω^k(U)⊕Ω^k(V)→Ω^k(U∩V) is exact at the first two nonzero terms.
items.strategy: Vanishing on the cover implies vanishing globally. Kernel of s means equality of the two restrictions; define the global form by either local value and verify smoothness in charts.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The de rham mayer vietoris difference map is surjective
items.statement: Under countable choice, s is surjective in every degree.
items.strategy: For subordinate ρ_U+ρ_V=1 take α=−ρ_Vω on U∩V, extended by zero to U, and β=ρ_Uω extended by zero to V. Supports contained in the opposite open set ensure smooth extension across artificial edges. Group the locally finite partition by the two cover members; the locally finite union of its closed supports is closed and still contained in that member. Then β−α=ω. Countable choice is used only for the partition theorem. For the exact countable-choice implementation of the partition supplier, use the set of ALL coordinate-ball/chart tuples with compact closure contained in U or V. For each member of a fixed countable basis which is contained in some eligible ball, select one eligible tuple containing it by countable choice. These selected balls cover M: each point has a basis neighbourhood inside an eligible ball. Repeat a member if a nonempty finite list needs indexing; M empty uses the empty family. Let H_r be the union of the first r compact closures. Choose each exhaustion index to be the least larger integer with H_r contained in the interior of the next H, so this recursion uses no dependent choice. For K_m the resulting exhaustion, the compact annulus K_m minus int K_(m-1) is covered by all pairs of nested coordinate neighbourhoods with closure W contained in V and closure V contained in a selected ball and in int K_(m+1) minus K_(m-2). Existence follows pointwise from coordinate balls and regularity, without choosing at all points. Countable choice selects one finite ordered covering list from the nonempty set of such lists for each annulus. Their outer neighbourhoods are locally finite by the annulus separation. Countable choice now supplies the compact-set bumps for that countable list; normalize their locally finite positive sum. Only the smooth quotient and support-inclusion clauses of the normalization lemma are used, not its phrase about subordination to a closed-support cover. Assign each support to U when contained in U and to V otherwise. The two grouped sums then have the closed support containment required above. This expands the existing partition route under the stated axiom without importing any unqualified point-indexed choice.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Short exact mayer vietoris sequence of de rham complexes
items.statement: Under countable choice, 0→Ω•(M)→Ω•(U)⊕Ω•(V)→Ω•(U∩V)→0 is a short exact sequence of cochain complexes.
items.strategy: Combine the degreewise exactness with restriction naturality. Finite direct sums are taken degreewise; no selection of arbitrary linear splittings is needed.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Mayer vietoris sequence in de rham cohomology
items.statement: Under countable choice, the two-open de Rham sequence is long exact, with δ:H^k(U∩V)→H^{k+1}(M).
items.strategy: Apply the earlier cohomology LES to the short exact sequence. Identify cohomology of the middle two-term direct sum componentwise; its cycle and boundary spaces are finite direct sums. Include the initial 0→H^0(M) term and zero negative degrees.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Explicit de rham mayer vietoris connecting class
items.statement: Under countable choice, For closed ω, δ[ω]=[η], where η|U=d(−ρ_Vω), η|V=d(ρ_Uω). This is independent of partition, lift and representative.
items.strategy: On the overlap the two derivatives agree because dω=0 and dρ_U=−dρ_V. Reindex the earlier module connector formula to cochains with no differential sign change. It identifies the glued η with δ and supplies independence. On the overlap η=dρ_U∧ω, with precisely this sign.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Naturality of de rham mayer vietoris for maps of covered manifolds
items.statement: Under countable choice, For F:M→N with F(U)⊂U′, F(V)⊂V′, pullbacks give a contravariant commutative ladder of the two Mayer–Vietoris sequences, including δ_M F_overlap*=F* δ_N.
items.strategy: Restrictions commute with pullback so both cochain squares commute using the same β−α sign. Apply the earlier naturality theorem after cochain reindexing. Alternatively pull back a lift and its differential to identify the connecting square; partitions need not be preserved.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham cohomology of a finite disjoint union is the direct sum
items.statement: For a finite disjoint union M=⊔_{j=1}^m M_j, restriction identifies H^k(M) with ⊕_j H^k(M_j).
items.strategy: Forms and d are componentwise; for a finite family choose primitives by finite choice only and identify kernels, images and quotients. For zero components both sides are zero. No arbitrary infinite product assertion is made.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham cohomology of spheres
items.statement: Under countable choice, for n≥1, H^k(S^n)=R in degrees 0 and n and zero otherwise; for S^0 it is R² in degree zero only.
items.strategy: Use U=S^n minus south pole and V=S^n minus north pole; stereographic formulas identify both with R^n. The overlap is S^{n−1}×R via x↦(x′/|x′|,x_{n+1}/|x′|), smoothly retracting to the equator. For n=1, s on H^0 is (a,b)↦(b−a,b−a) in R²; its cokernel is R and kernel diagonal R. For n≥2, overlap connected makes the H^0 difference map onto, hence H^1=0. For k≥2 use H^k(S^n)≅H^{k−1}(S^{n−1}) and induction. This does not use the later punctured-space computation or π_1(S^n).

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (2014)

items.title: De rham cohomology of punctured euclidean space
items.statement: Under countable choice, For n≥2, R^n\{0} has R in degrees 0,n−1 only. For n=1 it has R² in degree zero only; for n=0 all groups vanish.
items.strategy: Use the explicit smooth radial deformation F_t(x)=((1−t)+t/|x|)x, which never reaches zero. For n=1 use its two half-lines; n=0 is empty.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The de rham cohomology class of a form is defined without closedness
items.statement: False claim: every differential form represents a de Rham class.
items.strategy: On R², α=x dy has dα=dx∧dy≠0 and is not in the numerator of the quotient.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Every smooth form is either closed or exact
items.statement: False claim: every smooth form is closed or exact.
items.strategy: The same form x dy is not closed. Since exact forms are closed it cannot be exact either.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Continuously homotopic smooth maps can be inserted directly into the differential form homotopy operator
items.statement: False claim: the differential-form homotopy operator accepts an arbitrary continuous homotopy directly.
items.strategy: Take M a point and H(t)=|t−1/2| as a homotopy into R. It is continuous but has no differential at 1/2; pullback of dy as a smooth form on the cylinder is undefined. Smooth endpoints do not correct this regularity failure.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The poincare lemma says every closed form is globally exact
items.statement: False claim: Poincaré gives global exactness of every closed positive-degree form on every manifold.
items.strategy: For α=(x dy−y dx)/(x²+y²) on R²\{0}, compute dα=0 and pull back along (cos t,sin t), t∈[0,2π], to dt. Its period is 2π; an exact form has zero closed-loop period.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The mayer vietoris sequence is obtained by restricting forms without a partition of unity
items.statement: Under countable choice, Invalid proposed proof: restrictions alone establish the full Mayer–Vietoris sequence, with no proof of surjectivity of the difference map.
items.strategy: Restrictions give a complex and gluing gives middle exactness, but they provide no extension operator from an overlap. For U=(−∞,1), V=(0,∞), the overlap function 1/x cannot itself be smoothly extended to U across 0. The opposite cutoff construction supplies the missing lift. This refutes the naive extension recipe, NOT a claim that every possible proof must explicitly mention a partition.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham cohomology is a covariant functor
items.statement: False claim: the pullback construction is covariant.
items.strategy: For F:M→N the induced map has source H•(N) and target H•(M). With noncommuting self-maps of a finite discrete three-point manifold, pullback compositions reverse the order, as seen on characteristic functions.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

title: The De Rham Complex Homotopy and Mayer Vietoris — Examples

items.title: De rham cohomology of a point
items.statement: A point has de Rham ring R in degree zero only.
items.strategy: Its only nonzero form space is Ω^0=R and all differentials vanish.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham cohomology of euclidean space
items.statement: R^n has de Rham ring R in degree zero only, including n=0.
items.strategy: Apply radial contraction and the positive-degree formula; constants give degree zero.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (2014)

items.title: De rham cohomology of a finite discrete manifold
items.statement: An m-point discrete manifold has H^0=R^m with componentwise multiplication and no positive-degree cohomology.
items.strategy: All tangent spaces are zero; use the finite disjoint-union result, including m=0.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham cohomology of the circle from mayer vietoris
items.statement: Under countable choice, H^0(S¹)=H^1(S¹)=R and all other groups vanish.
items.strategy: Choose the two complementary-pole arcs. Their overlap consists of two contractible intervals, and the degree-zero difference map R²→R² is (a,b)↦(b−a,b−a). Its cokernel is one-dimensional.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The angular form generates the first de rham cohomology of the circle
items.statement: Under countable choice, The class of (x dy−y dx)/(2π) restricted to the unit circle generates H^1(S¹), with period one.
items.strategy: Parametrize by (cos t,sin t): the pullback is dt/(2π) and its integral is one. Stokes obstructs exactness, and the already proved group has dimension one.

references.title: Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (2014)
John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham cohomology of the two sphere
items.statement: Under countable choice, S² has H^0=H²=R and H¹=0.
items.strategy: Use the n=2 case of the sphere theorem; identify the overlap with S¹×R to display the nonzero connecting map.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The standard volume form generates top cohomology of a sphere
items.statement: Under countable choice, For n≥1 the standard outward sphere form ω=Σ_i(−1)^{i−1}x_i dx_1∧⋯∧omit(dx_i)∧⋯∧dx_{n+1}|S^n generates H^n(S^n).
items.strategy: Evaluate it on outward-oriented tangent bases: it is positive and nowhere zero. Compactness makes its integral finite and positivity makes it nonzero. It cannot be exact by Stokes; H^n is one-dimensional. No later Riemannian volume item is used.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: De rham cohomology of punctured three space
items.statement: Under countable choice, R³\{0} has R in degrees zero and two only.
items.strategy: Write the radial retraction explicitly and apply the punctured-space theorem.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Homotopy equivalent annulus and circle have isomorphic de rham rings
items.statement: Under countable choice, An annulus {a<|x|<b}, 0<a<1<b, and the circle have isomorphic de Rham graded rings.
items.strategy: The positive radial homotopy to |x|=1 stays between the starting and final radii; inclusion and retraction are smooth homotopy inverses. Multiplication is preserved; the degree-one generator squares to zero.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The closed angular form on the punctured plane is not exact
items.statement: The angular form (x dy−y dx)/(x²+y²) on the punctured plane is closed but not exact.
items.strategy: Differentiate the two coefficients to get dα=0. Its pullback to the unit-circle parametrization is dt, giving period 2π.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The pullback on cohomology reverses composition order
items.statement: Pullback composition cannot be treated as covariant.
items.strategy: On three discrete points choose F swapping 1,2 and G swapping 2,3. For f the indicator of point 1, (F*G*f)(2)=1 while (G*F*f)(2)=0. This follows by evaluating f∘G∘F and f∘F∘G. In general (G∘F)*=F*G*.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: An explicit mayer vietoris connecting form on the circle
items.statement: Under countable choice, The circle Mayer–Vietoris connector has an explicit nonzero representative from a locally constant overlap function.
items.strategy: Cover by complementary-pole arcs. Give the overlap components values 0 and 1 for ω. Choose a subordinate partition and put η|U=−dρ_V ω, η|V=dρ_U ω. This smooth global one-form represents δ[ω]; (0,1) is outside the diagonal image, so exactness proves the class nonzero. Any period normalization is stated with the chosen orientation and component order.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

title: Riemannian Metrics Length Distance and Volume

items.title: Riemannian metric and riemannian manifold
items.statement: A Riemannian metric is a smooth symmetric positive-definite covariant 2-tensor on a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold. Dimension zero is allowed; boundaries are allowed when explicitly used.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Ved Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry, September 2025

items.title: Coordinate criterion for a riemannian metric
items.statement: A local tensor g=g_ij dx^i⊗dx^j is Riemannian iff G=(g_ij) is smooth symmetric positive definite; coordinate matrices obey G_y=J^T G_x J, J=∂x/∂y.
items.strategy: Apply the tensor transformation rule and evaluate on coordinate vectors. Congruence by an invertible Jacobian preserves symmetry and positive definiteness.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Ved Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry, September 2025

items.title: Every smooth manifold admits a riemannian metric
items.statement: Under countable choice every smooth manifold admits a Riemannian metric.
items.strategy: Apply the earlier bundle-metric theorem to TM. Use the following exact countable-choice implementation of its local-frame and partition selections. For manifolds with boundary use the boundary tangent bundle and boundary partition suppliers explicitly when authoring that extension. For the boundary case, apply the boundary tangent-bundle and partition results to the same countable local-frame metric construction; finite positive weighted sums prove positivity and local finiteness proves smoothness. Take all admissible trivialization/chart tuples with relatively compact nested coordinate balls (half-balls at boundary), rather than choosing a chart at every point. For each member of a countable basis contained in some eligible ball choose one eligible tuple by countable choice; these balls cover M. On this countable cover form finite unions of compact closures and take least increasing exhaustion indices with each union inside the interior of the next. For each compact annulus take the set of all finite ordered lists of nested coordinate neighbourhoods whose inner sets cover the annulus and whose outer compact closures lie in a cover member and in the adjacent open annular band. This set is nonempty by finite compactness and local coordinate regularity. Countable choice selects those lists for all annuli; their outer domains are locally finite by separation of the bands. Select the countable bump family by countable choice, using Euclidean bumps restricted to the half-space at boundary, and divide by its smooth positive sum. The resulting weights have closed supports in their labelled trivializations, so multiplying the local Euclidean frame metrics and extending by zero is smooth. This uses the normalization lemma only for smoothness, positivity and support inclusion, not for its closed-cover subordination wording. Empty M uses the unique empty metric, and rank zero uses the zero fibre metric. All selections are countable families of nonempty sets after the least-index exhaustion recursion; no point-indexed AC or dependent choice is used.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Ved Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry, September 2025

items.title: Pullback riemannian metric
items.statement: For smooth F:M→N and Riemannian h, define the pullback tensor (F*h)_p(v,w)=h_{F(p)}(dF_pv,dF_pw); positivity is not built into this definition.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Pullback of a riemannian metric is riemannian exactly for immersions
items.statement: F*h is Riemannian exactly when F is an immersion; otherwise it is positive semidefinite with kernel ker dF.
items.strategy: Smoothness and symmetry follow from tensor pullback. The quadratic value is |dF(v)|², strictly positive for all nonzero v exactly when dF is injective at every point.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian isometry and local isometry
items.statement: An isometry is a diffeomorphism F with F*h=g. A local isometry is a smooth local diffeomorphism with F*h=g; on boundaryless manifolds, equivalently a smooth metric-preserving map between equal-dimensional manifolds. An isometric immersion is separately defined and need not be a local isometry.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian isometries form a group and local isometries are local diffeomorphisms
items.statement: Isometries of a fixed Riemannian manifold form a group; equal-dimensional metric-preserving smooth maps between boundaryless manifolds are local diffeomorphisms.
items.strategy: Pullback identities give closure, identity and inverse. In equal dimension positivity makes dF invertible; apply the inverse function theorem. For boundary manifolds the equivalent differential criterion also requires the appropriate boundary-preserving local chart hypothesis; use the local-diffeomorphism definition there.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Conformal equivalence of riemannian metrics
items.statement: Metrics g and g̃ are conformally equivalent if g̃=e^{2u}g for a smooth real u; this is positive smooth rescaling.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Pointwise norm and angle from a riemannian metric
items.statement: |v|_g=√g(v,v). For nonzero v,w, angle θ∈[0,π] satisfies cos θ=g(v,w)/(|v||w|); endpoints 0,π are allowed.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Ved Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry, September 2025

items.title: Musical isomorphisms
items.statement: The musical maps are v♭=g(v,·) and its pointwise inverse α♯, characterized by g(α♯,v)=α(v). Smoothness is discharged next.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The musical maps are smooth inverse bundle isomorphisms
items.statement: ♭:TM→T*M and ♯:T*M→TM are smooth inverse bundle isomorphisms.
items.strategy: G is invertible by positive definiteness. In coordinates ♭ uses G and ♯ uses G^{-1}=adj(G)/det G, whose entries are smooth since det G>0. These intrinsic inverse maps therefore glue.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Ved Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry, September 2025

items.title: Riemannian gradient
items.statement: For smooth f define grad_g f=(df)♯, a smooth vector field.

references.title: Ved Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry, September 2025
John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The gradient is characterized by inner products
items.statement: The gradient is the unique smooth vector field with g(grad_g f,X)=Xf for every smooth vector field X.
items.strategy: Apply the defining inverse pairing of ♯ pointwise. Uniqueness follows from nondegeneracy, testing all tangent vectors via local coordinate fields.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian metrics induce metrics on dual tensor and exterior bundles
items.statement: g induces smooth metrics on duals, tensor bundles and exterior powers. On wedge decomposables the exterior metric is det(⟨α_i,β_j⟩), so increasing orthonormal wedge monomials have norm one.
items.strategy: Define dual metric through ♯ and tensor metric by products. The determinant pairing is alternating in both lists and descends through exterior universal properties; in an orthonormal basis it is the identity matrix. Changes of orthonormal frame preserve the construction. Smooth Gram-Schmidt is local: subtract earlier projections and divide by positive smooth norms. Do not inherit the unnormalized restricted tensor metric, which differs by k!.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Ved Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry, September 2025

items.title: Piecewise c one curve on a manifold
items.statement: A piecewise C¹ manifold curve is continuous on a compact interval with a finite subdivision on whose closed pieces it is C¹ in charts, including one-sided endpoint derivatives. This does not require nonzero speed.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian speed and length
items.statement: Speed is |γ′(t)|_g on each smooth piece, and L_g(γ) is the sum of its Riemann integrals. The finitely many corner values do not affect length.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Ved Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry, September 2025

items.title: Riemannian length is independent of piecewise c one subdivision
items.statement: Riemannian length is independent of subdivision and of corner derivative conventions.
items.strategy: Pass to the finite common refinement; additivity of the scalar Riemann integral and invariance under finitely many point changes give equality.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian length is invariant under orientation preserving piecewise c one reparametrization
items.statement: If φ:[c,d]→[a,b] is a continuous nondecreasing surjection, piecewise C¹, then γ∘φ is piecewise C¹ and L_g(γ∘φ)=L_g(γ). In particular orientation-preserving piecewise C¹ reparametrizations preserve length; pauses are allowed.
items.strategy: Refine at breakpoints of φ and the interval fibres over the finitely many breakpoints of γ. On intervals mapped into one C¹ piece use the chain rule and the substitution theorem with φ′≥0. A nontrivial fibre is a constant interval and contributes zero. There are finitely many such refinements. Sum the equalities; no division by φ′ is used.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Length is additive under concatenation and invariant under reversal
items.statement: Length adds under finite concatenation and is unchanged by reversal.
items.strategy: Apply integral additivity to the two concatenated parameter pieces; affine parameter changes preserve length. Reversal changes the velocity sign but not its norm.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Local comparison of a riemannian metric with the euclidean metric
items.statement: For compact K in a single chart and n≥1, constants 0<c≤C satisfy c|v|²≤g_x(v,v)≤C|v|² on K. Dimension zero is vacuous.
items.strategy: On compact K×S^{n−1}, the continuous positive function (x,v)↦g_x(v,v) attains a positive minimum and finite maximum; scale by |v|². Choose a closed coordinate ball contained in the chart before applying this neighbourhood estimate. This avoids importing an eigenvalue-continuity theorem. If K is empty choose c=C=1. Otherwise K×S^{n−1} is a nonempty Euclidean compact set and the topology/metric compactness agreement supplies the precise EVT hypothesis.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Any two points in a connected smooth manifold can be joined by a piecewise c one curve
items.statement: Any two points in a connected nonempty smooth manifold can be joined by a finite piecewise C¹ curve.
items.strategy: Fix p. The points reachable by finite coordinate segments form an open set, because coordinate balls (relative half-balls at a boundary) are convex. Every other reachability class is also open by the same argument; connectedness leaves one class. This avoids a choice of an infinite chain of charts.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian distance on a connected manifold
items.statement: On connected M define d_g(p,q)=inf{L_g(γ): γ piecewise C¹ from p to q}. The family is nonempty, finite-valued and bounded below by zero.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian distance is a metric
items.statement: d_g is a finite metric on connected M.
items.strategy: Constant paths and reversal give the first axioms. Choose two ε-competitive paths for the triangle inequality and concatenate; finite choice suffices. For p≠q take a coordinate ball centred at p whose compact closure is inside a chart and excludes q. Every competitor exits this ball; up to its first exit, length is at least √c times the Euclidean endpoint displacement, hence at least √c r>0. Existence of the exit time follows from continuity on the compact parameter interval. In a connected zero-manifold there is one point.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The riemannian distance topology is the manifold topology
items.statement: The metric topology of d_g equals the manifold topology.
items.strategy: For a coordinate ball of radius r about p, the first-exit estimate puts B_d(p,√c r) inside that ball. Conversely, coordinate straight segments within a convex smaller ball have length at most √C|x−x(p)|, so sufficiently small coordinate balls lie in any prescribed metric ball. Both estimates use compact chart closures, not arbitrary relatively compact sets.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Length dominates endpoint distance
items.statement: For any competitor γ, d_g(γ(a),γ(b))≤L_g(γ).
items.strategy: The infimum of the nonempty length set is bounded above by each of its elements.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: A smooth map with pointwise operator norm at most c is c lipschitz for riemannian distance
items.statement: For connected Riemannian M,N, smooth F:M→N and finite c≥0 with |dF_pv|≤c|v| for every p,v, d_h(Fp,Fq)≤c d_g(p,q).
items.strategy: Push every competing path forward. Chain rule bounds its speed and its length by c times the original length. Take infima; for c=0 the bound forces target distance zero directly.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian isometries preserve length and distance
items.statement: Riemannian isometries preserve lengths and distances on each connected component.
items.strategy: Pullback equality gives equal speeds. Apply the Lipschitz result with c=1 to F and F^{-1}; a diffeomorphism permutes components.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Extended riemannian distance on a disconnected manifold
items.statement: On arbitrary M take the componentwise Riemannian distance within each component and +∞ between distinct components. This is an extended metric, not a finite-valued metric; inf ∅=+∞.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Distance from a point to a subset
items.statement: For A⊂M define d_g(x,A)=inf_{a∈A}d_g(x,a), with inf ∅=+∞. In a component C meeting A this equals the finite distance to A∩C.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Distance to a nonempty subset is one lipschitz
items.statement: For A nonempty in connected M, distance to A is finite and 1-Lipschitz. More generally the same holds on C when A∩C≠∅.
items.strategy: For a∈A∩C the triangle inequality gives d(x,a)≤d(x,y)+d(y,a); take infima and then interchange x,y. No subtraction of infinite values occurs; components missing A have the constant extended value +∞.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian volume density
items.statement: The Riemannian density is μ_g=√det(G_x)|dx¹⋯dxⁿ|. For n=0 take det(empty)=1, so each point has weight one; no orientation is needed.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The riemannian volume density is coordinate independent
items.statement: The local Riemannian densities glue to a positive smooth density.
items.strategy: For J=∂x/∂y, det G_y=(det J)²det G_x, hence √det G_y=|det J|√det G_x. This is exactly the density transition law, including positive smoothness.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian volume form on an oriented manifold
items.statement: On oriented M the Riemannian volume form is vol_g=√det G dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ in positive charts when n≥1. In dimension zero it is the supplied orientation sign ±1 at each point; μ_g=|vol_g|.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Ved Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry, September 2025

items.title: The riemannian volume form is the unique positive unit top form
items.statement: vol_g is the unique positive unit section of Λ^n T*M for the chosen orientation.
items.strategy: Use the normalized exterior metric: an oriented orthonormal coframe has unit wedge, and any top form is its scalar multiple. Positivity and norm one force scalar 1. In dimension zero the orientation sign specifies the positive ray in Λ^0=R.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian volume of a compactly supported smooth density
items.statement: Under countable choice, for smooth compactly supported f define ∫_M f μ_g by the earlier density integral. More generally a compactly supported signed smooth density σ has its existing intrinsic integral, independently of g. Countable choice is inherited from the chart-partition construction in def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density; no choice-free existence assertion is made.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian volume is the radon measure of the riemannian density
items.statement: Under countable choice, μ_g defines a compact-finite, locally finite, sigma-finite Radon Borel measure vol_g(A). Its completion has a separately specified completed domain. Smooth compact-support integrals agree with the earlier density integral; metric balls are Borel.
items.strategy: Apply the two exact earlier density-measure suppliers to the positive smooth density. The topology theorem makes componentwise metric balls open in the manifold topology, so they are Borel. Arbitrary volume may be infinite; dimension zero gives counting measure. Completion and countable chart gluing carry the stated countable-choice cost.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian divergence
items.statement: Define div_g X locally by L_X vol_g=(div_g X)vol_g. On nonorientable M choose local orientations: reversing one multiplies both sides by −1, so the scalar glues. Equivalently it is the Lie derivative of the positive density divided by that density.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Coordinate formula for riemannian divergence
items.strategy: Substitute √det G for the local coefficient in the earlier volume-form divergence formula. The orientation-change cancellation proves that the same scalar works on every chart, including nonorientable M. In dimension zero the empty sum is zero.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian divergence theorem
items.statement: Assume countable choice (AC_omega). On an oriented Riemannian manifold with boundary of dimension n≥1 and a smooth compactly supported vector field X, ∫_M div_g X vol_g=∫_{∂M}g(X,ν)vol_{∂g}, with outward unit normal ν and outward-normal-first boundary orientation.
items.strategy: Locally define ν by the normalized negative g-gradient of an inward-positive boundary coordinate; independence follows from uniqueness of the outward unit normal in the one-dimensional orthogonal complement. The induced boundary metric is positive by immersion. In an oriented orthonormal boundary frame, ι_X vol_g restricts to g(X,ν)vol_{∂g}; Stokes applied to this compactly supported (n−1)-form gives the result. For n=1 the induced boundary zero-form is the determinant-line orientation sign; the signed boundary integral gives endpoint subtraction. Countable choice is used at the global chart-partition/localization and integration step inherited from thm-general-stokes-theorem and thm-divergence-theorem-relative-to-a-volume-form; the normal construction and pointwise contraction identity introduce no additional choice. Empty boundary and zero field give zero; compact M allows every smooth X. This is a sufficient inherited assumption, not a necessity claim.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian hodge star
items.statement: On an oriented Riemannian n-manifold, *:Λ^kT*M→Λ^{n−k}T*M is characterized by α∧*β=⟨α,β⟩vol_g for every α,β of degree k. This is the untwisted, orientation-dependent convention.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Hodge star is a smooth bundle isomorphism
items.statement: The Hodge star exists uniquely and is a smooth bundle isomorphism.
items.strategy: Construct a local oriented orthonormal coframe by smooth Gram-Schmidt; put *e^I=sgn(I,I^c)e^{I^c}. Pairing with all e^J verifies the defining equation. The wedge pairing is nondegenerate by the complementary-basis formula, so uniqueness forces agreement across frames; entries are smooth. It is a signed permutation matrix. For n=0 it multiplies by the supplied orientation sign.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Hodge star squared sign
items.statement: On k-forms, **=(-1)^{k(n−k)}id.
items.strategy: The two complement permutations differ by exchanging blocks of lengths k,n−k, requiring k(n−k) transpositions. Apply on the wedge basis, then use linearity; also k=0,n and n=0.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian inner product of compactly supported forms
items.statement: Under countable choice, on an oriented Riemannian manifold, (α,β)=∫_M α∧*β is a positive-definite inner product on compactly supported real smooth k-forms, 0≤k≤dim M.
items.strategy: The integrand equals ⟨α,β⟩vol_g, so the integral is bilinear and symmetric. A nonzero α has positive squared norm on a neighbourhood; its nonnegative compactly supported squared norm therefore has strictly positive integral. Finite dimension-zero sums obey the same conclusion. Countable choice is used precisely when obtaining the chart partition for the earlier density integral, not in the pointwise Hodge-star algebra. On a nonorientable manifold only the separately defined density pairing is available; the displayed top-form formula assumes orientation.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The codifferential and hodge theory
items.statement: The codifferential, its analytic adjoint interpretation, Laplacian, harmonic theory and Hodge decomposition belong to later Hodge/PDE work. No such result is assumed here.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The pullback of a riemannian metric by every smooth map is a riemannian metric
items.statement: False claim: every smooth pullback of a Riemannian metric is Riemannian.
items.strategy: A constant map R→R pulls dx² back to zero; its differential has nontrivial kernel.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Every riemannian manifold has finite distance between points in different components
items.statement: False claim: different components always have finite Riemannian distance.
items.strategy: On the disjoint union of two Euclidean lines no continuous curve connects points in opposite components. The admissible family is empty and its infimum is +∞.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Riemannian distance is defined by the length of a unique shortest curve
items.statement: False claim: distance is defined by a unique shortest curve. Both existence and uniqueness can fail.
items.strategy: Existence: in R²\{0}, between (−1,0) and (1,0), Euclidean length is at least 2; a segment with a semicircle detour of radius ε has length 2+(π−2)ε, so infimum 2. Equality in the projection length bound forces a straight monotone horizontal path through the excluded origin, impossible. Uniqueness: on the unit circle antipodal endpoints have two semicircles of length π; subdividing any path into finitely many angle charts constructs an angle lift, whose total variation is at least π. Thus both attain the infimum without using geodesic theory.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The riemannian volume form exists on every riemannian manifold
items.statement: False claim: every Riemannian manifold has an ordinary positive global Riemannian volume form.
items.strategy: Use the explicit open Möbius strip (t,s)~(t+1,−s): Euclidean dt²+ds² descends, but a putative nonvanishing top form f(t,s)dt∧ds must satisfy f(t+1,−s)=−f(t,s). On s=0 continuity forces a zero between t and t+1. The positive density descends because the absolute Jacobian is one. Supply the quotient atlas explicitly: boxes of t-width less than one project injectively, transitions are (t,s)↦(t+m,(−1)^m s), and a countable rational-box basis descends. Disjoint small boxes separate distinct orbits (only finitely many integer translates can meet bounded boxes), proving Hausdorffness. Thus this construction does not depend on a B-page Möbius-band item.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The distance function is smooth on all of m times m
items.statement: False claim: Riemannian distance is smooth everywhere on M×M.
items.strategy: On the Euclidean real line d(x,y)=|x−y| by the integral endpoint bound and the straight segment. Restricting y=0 gives |x|, not differentiable at zero. No cut-locus theorem is imported.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The hodge star is defined without an orientation
items.statement: False claim: the ordinary Hodge star requires no orientation.
items.strategy: Already on a Euclidean line *1=dx in the positive orientation and *1=−dx in the opposite orientation. A metric alone does not distinguish them; an orientation-twisted alternative is a different convention.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

title: Riemannian Metrics Length Distance and Volume — Examples

items.title: The euclidean metric and its musical maps
items.statement: For Euclidean g, v♭=Σv_i dx^i, α♯=Σα_i∂_i, grad f=Σ∂_if ∂_i.
items.strategy: G and G^{-1} are both the identity; substitute in the musical formulas.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
Ved Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry, September 2025

items.title: The round metric on the sphere as an induced metric
items.statement: The unit sphere has the round metric induced by its Euclidean inclusion.
items.strategy: Its differential includes the tangent hyperplane, hence is injective. On S² off the poles, x=(sinθ cosφ,sinθ sinφ,cosθ) gives g=dθ²+sin²θ dφ². Coordinate degeneracy at poles is not tensor degeneracy.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The product riemannian metric
items.statement: The product metric is π_M*g+π_N*h, represented by diag(G,H).
items.strategy: Evaluate on (v,w): g(v,v)+h(w,w)>0 for any nonzero pair, and the block coefficients are smooth. The tensor is a sum of pullbacks, not a tensor product.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: A conformal metric on the plane
items.statement: For g=e^{2u}(dx²+dy²), grad_g f=e^{−2u}(f_x∂_x+f_y∂_y) and μ_g=e^{2u}|dxdy|.
items.strategy: Invert the diagonal matrix and take the positive square root of its determinant.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The hyperbolic upper half space metric
items.statement: On {y>0}⊂R^n, g=y^{−2}(Σ_{i<n}dx_i²+dy²) is a smooth Riemannian metric with density y^{−n}|dx_1⋯dx_{n−1}dy|.
items.strategy: All eigenvalues are y^{−2}>0 and the determinant is y^{−2n}. No curvature or completeness statement is asserted.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: The flat torus metric from periodic euclidean coordinates
items.statement: Periodic Euclidean coordinates define the flat metric on (R/Z)^n.
items.strategy: Use small translated boxes with transition maps integer translations; their derivative matrices are identity, so Σdx_i² glues. This proves the particular quotient atlas directly; no general Riemannian quotient theorem is used.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Length and distance on the circle
items.statement: On the unit circle, distance is the smaller angular separation; antipodes have two distinct shortest semicircles.
items.strategy: Lift a piecewise C¹ path to an angle by finitely many local angle charts along its compact parameter interval, adjusting by integer multiples of 2π on overlaps. Its length is ∫|θ′|≥|θ(b)−θ(a)|. Endpoint lifts differ by the endpoint angle plus 2πk; minimize over k. The shorter circular arc attains that minimum.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: A riemannian distance with no cross component finite value
items.statement: On two disjoint Euclidean lines the extended distance between the two components is +∞.
items.strategy: A continuous path image is connected and cannot meet both open-and-closed components. Within each line the distance is ordinary absolute difference.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Volume density in polar coordinates
items.statement: The Euclidean plane has density r|dr dθ| and positive-oriented volume r dr∧dθ on polar charts r>0.
items.strategy: Differentiate x=r cosθ,y=r sinθ to get diag(1,r²) and square root determinant r. The coordinate chart excludes r=0 and uses an angular interval.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Hodge star on euclidean three space
items.statement: In standard oriented Euclidean R³: *1=dx∧dy∧dz, *dx=dy∧dz, *dy=dz∧dx, *dz=dx∧dy and **=id in all degrees.
items.strategy: Use complementary increasing wedge monomials and permutation signs. In particular *(dx∧dy)=dz and *(dx∧dz)=−dy.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: Divergence in polar coordinates
items.statement: In plane polar coordinates div_g(X^r∂_r+X^θ∂_θ)=r^{−1}∂_r(rX^r)+∂_θX^θ.
items.strategy: Substitute √det G=r. If physical orthonormal components are used instead, the angular coefficient is rX^θ; record this conversion to avoid a spurious extra factor.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition

items.title: A degenerate pullback metric under a constant map
items.statement: For a constant map F:M→R from a smooth manifold of dimension n>0, the pullback F*(dx²) is zero. It is not Riemannian exactly when M is nonempty; for M empty it is vacuously a Riemannian metric. In particular F:R→R, F(x)=0 gives a degenerate pullback.
items.strategy: The differential of a constant coordinate expression is zero, so the pullback tensor vanishes. If M is nonempty, choose one point and one chart; its first coordinate tangent vector is nonzero since n>0 and has zero quadratic value. If M is empty there are no tangent vectors at points to test, so smoothness and positive definiteness are vacuous. The concrete source R supplies the required counterexample without choice.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
